The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.60 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider and the driver: this is a provisional automated ruling. THE MEASUREMENTS. The GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0) measures 34.17 km between pickup and dropoff. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern; the 34.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00104) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. The booked optimal route was 27.1 km, so the measured excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal — above both the 20% and the 0.8 km tests, so a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. THE CLOSURE EXPLAINS MOST OF IT. The driver's account of an accident is corroborated by the LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0): a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit — the expressway the booked optimal route uses ('PIE westbound throughout') — active 20:02–21:35, which covers the trip, with the trace showing the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. Exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07 km, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal route is 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. THE REFUND. POL-RD-03 provides that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route. Run on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00104, weight 1.0; fare_model METERED, surge multiplier 1.0 read from that artifact): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828. Refund = charged_total 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. THE DRIVER'S NO_ACTION ARGUMENT IS REJECTED. It is correct that 2.17 km (6.8%) of excess remains against the adjusted optimal, but POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation on the trip as driven against the booked optimal (7.07 km, 26.09%), and POL-RD-03 expressly refunds the excess beyond its cap under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted route. The 2.17 km the driver drove beyond what the closure justifies is the driver's own responsibility, not the rider's. THE RIDER'S CLAIM OF ABOUT $14 IS NOT SUPPORTED. The rider is right that 34 km is far longer than her usual 27 km and that $43.41 is about $14 above her normal fare; but a documented closure justified 4.90 km of that excess, so only the excess beyond it is refunded. OTHER CLAIMS. POL-RD-04 moves no distance: the only route-proposing message is the driver's own ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'), and the rider's reply 'ok but not too long ah' names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so there is no rider instruction to exclude distance for. The second advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired and that impairment is disclosed: weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; it is rejected on the merits because it describes a breakdown on the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters, so it excuses nothing — and because it is present in the bundle and overlaps the trip window, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips in 90 days (ratio 0.0035, below 0.05), the excess is not material (7.07 km is under 8.0 km and 26.09% is under 50%), and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a context-only field under POL-GEN-01 that may not be substituted for the trailing-window figure named by POL-RD-06. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: there is no ERP, no airport surcharge on a trip originating at Tampines, and no unmatched charge line. POL-RD-11 does not apply because the fare model is METERED with no quoted fare. NO ESCALATION. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s), so the independent-corroboration requirement of POL-RD-07 does not arise and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, no timestamps conflict, the refund is far below SGD 150, and the second advisory is disposed of on the merits. The case is decided on the evidence, not held. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept This trip's own telemetry establishes the deviation. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and the trace records 34.17 km against the 27.1 km booked optimal — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%, which clears both establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute). The rounded 34.2 km on the trip record is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, but the two agree in substance, so the rider's account of a trip roughly a quarter longer than the route she has taken dozens of times is made out on the platform's own data.

evidence EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The driver's PIE advisory excuses only a capped part of that excess. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative - booked optimal) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. The remaining 2.17 km is unexplained on any clause in the policy: the driver drove 34.17 km when the shortest lawful alternative around the closure was 30.1 km, and the rider had asked him in chat to keep it short. Nothing in POL-RD-03, and no other clause on the record, licenses the excess beyond 4.90 km.

evidence EV-GPS-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-CHAT-00104 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-RD-01

kept The refund is then arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the closure-adjusted optimal route because POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess: charged_total 43.41; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 km + 0.28 x 40.1 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828; refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare = 3.582, which rounds up to a payable of SGD 3.60. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND: it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so neither NO_ACTION nor FULL_REFUND follows.

evidence EV-FARE-00104, EV-GPS-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01, EV-TRIP-00104 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-03

kept Nothing on this record closes off the distance refund. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and the rider is not confined to pass-through corrections: POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and the recomputation above is the figure the ruling must state.

evidence EV-FARE-00104 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-11

kept The driver cannot move his detour onto the rider. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction, and there is no rider instruction here: the only route-proposing message on the log is the driver's own at 20:38:12 ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'), and the rider's single reply, 'ok but not too long ah', is an acknowledgment carrying a limit — it comes after the choice was announced, it names no road, and it carries no waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are not met, so no distance is excluded from the excess on this ground, and the driver's own selection of ECP, MCE and the AYE beyond the closure stands unexcused.

evidence EV-CHAT-00104, EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-08

EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: admissibility weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. It describes a breakdown on the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters — intersects_route is false and the trace carries no fix inside its geometry — and it was entered by the operator rather than ingested from the LTA feed. POL-RD-03 exonerates only an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so the driver's CTE assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and reduces no part of the excess.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00104-02, EV-GPS-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-GEN-02, POL-RD-08

The most he can do is the PIE advisory, and that is capped, so nothing outside the 4.90 km exonerated band is taken off the excess.

The driver advocate

kept The LTA DataMall collision in EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) satisfies every limb of POL-RD-03. It names a road the booked optimal route traverses - 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Eunos Link exit', and the optimal route source on the trip record is 'PIE westbound throughout'. Its validity window, 20:02 to 21:35 on 16 July 2026, straddles the trip's 20:35:10 to 21:22:10 running time with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end. And the trace matches it: the vehicle leaves the PIE at the Bedok North Ave 4 exit ahead of the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE, with derived.advisory_area recording trace_enters_area true, 24 fixes inside the advisory box and a minimum distance to it of 0 m.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00104-01, EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104 · clauses POL-RD-03

kept The exoneration is capped as POL-RD-03 requires, and the cap does real work here: justified excess = min(measured 7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal route is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 min to 40.1 min. On this trip 4.90 km of the 7.07 km excess is exonerated because the driver correctly avoided a HIGH-severity closure on the very expressway the optimal route uses.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00104-01, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 · clauses POL-RD-03

kept Once POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 requires optimal_distance_km to be measured as the adjusted optimal that clause produces, and it requires the trace figure to govern, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 34.17 km. Against the closure-adjusted 32.00 km the excess is 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of optimal. The absolute limb (greater than 0.8 km) is met but the percentage limb (greater than 20%) fails, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH to pass. No deviation is established, so the outcome is NO_ACTION, which on this rider-filed dispute leaves the CHARGED fare and the nil refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand (POL-GEN-03 is party-relative: the charge stays in place).

evidence EV-GPS-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-TRIP-00104 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-GEN-03

Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver: this is a provisional automated ruling. THE MEASUREMENTS. The GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0) measures 34.17 km between pickup and dropoff. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern; the 34.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00104) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. The booked optimal route was 27.1 km, so the measured excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal — above both the 20% and the 0.8 km tests, so a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. THE CLOSURE EXPLAINS MOST OF IT. The driver's account of an accident is corroborated by the LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0): a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit — the expressway the booked optimal route uses ('PIE westbound throughout') — active 20:02–21:35, which covers the trip, with the trace showing the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. Exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07 km, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal route is 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. THE REFUND. POL-RD-03 provides that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route. Run on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00104, weight 1.0; fare_model METERED, surge multiplier 1.0 read from that artifact): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828. Refund = charged_total 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. THE DRIVER'S NO_ACTION ARGUMENT IS REJECTED. It is correct that 2.17 km (6.8%) of excess remains against the adjusted optimal, but POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation on the trip as driven against the booked optimal (7.07 km, 26.09%), and POL-RD-03 expressly refunds the excess beyond its cap under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted route. The 2.17 km the driver drove beyond what the closure justifies is the driver's own responsibility, not the rider's. THE RIDER'S CLAIM OF ABOUT $14 IS NOT SUPPORTED. The rider is right that 34 km is far longer than her usual 27 km and that $43.41 is about $14 above her normal fare; but a documented closure justified 4.90 km of that excess, so only the excess beyond it is refunded. OTHER CLAIMS. POL-RD-04 moves no distance: the only route-proposing message is the driver's own ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'), and the rider's reply 'ok but not too long ah' names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so there is no rider instruction to exclude distance for. The second advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired and that impairment is disclosed: weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; it is rejected on the merits because it describes a breakdown on the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters, so it excuses nothing — and because it is present in the bundle and overlaps the trip window, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips in 90 days (ratio 0.0035, below 0.05), the excess is not material (7.07 km is under 8.0 km and 26.09% is under 50%), and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a context-only field under POL-GEN-01 that may not be substituted for the trailing-window figure named by POL-RD-06. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: there is no ERP, no airport surcharge on a trip originating at Tampines, and no unmatched charge line. POL-RD-11 does not apply because the fare model is METERED with no quoted fare. NO ESCALATION. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s), so the independent-corroboration requirement of POL-RD-07 does not arise and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, no timestamps conflict, the refund is far below SGD 150, and the second advisory is disposed of on the merits. The case is decided on the evidence, not held. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
Both of you: this is my ruling on trip TRP-00104 of 16 July 2026, Tampines (Our Tampines Hub) to one-north. The deviation was real, but the driver's explanation for most of it is good, so the rider gets a small refund, not the $14 she asked for. 1. The measurement (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0, 283 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps) records 34.17 km; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-00104) was 27.1 km. I use the trace figure, not the rounded 34.2 km copy, because POL-RD-01 says the trace governs. The excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20%, over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows from it. 2. The driver's partial excuse (POL-RD-03). The LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos, which is the expressway the booked optimal route uses; its window 20:02-21:35 straddles the 20:35-21:22 trip; and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE. That satisfies POL-RD-03. The exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. So 4.90 km of the 7.07 km is excused; the remaining 2.17 km is not. 3. The driver's NO_ACTION submission is refused. The argument that, measured against the adjusted 32.00 km, the remaining 2.17 km is only 6.8% and so fails POL-RD-01, leaving nothing payable, is rejected. The deviation is established on the excess as driven from the booked optimal, and POL-RD-03 itself directs that the excess beyond its cap 'is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route'. To let the establishment test swallow that direction would make the cap and the adjusted-route refund dead letters. The driver is not penalised for avoiding the closure; he accounts for the 2.17 km driven beyond even the capped allowance. 4. The driver's CTE breakdown excuse fails. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired (weight_multiplier 0.25; issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED, UNVERIFIED_SOURCE), and in any case it describes the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters (intersects_route false; no fix inside its box). POL-RD-03(a) is not met, so it excuses nothing. Because it is present in the pool and its window covers the trip, its rejection is on the merits and is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; it simply carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. The finding does not rest on that artifact, so its discount does not lower confidence. 5. The rider's further points. The ECP/MCE/AYE route was not rider-requested: the only route proposal in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00104) is the driver's own ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' is an acknowledgment, not an instruction with a road or waypoint, so no distance is excluded under POL-RD-04. POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model on EV-FARE-00104 is METERED with no quoted fare. No corroboration condition attaches to the rider: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, well below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08. 6. The money (POL-RD-02), computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total = 43.41. Refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of $3.60. 7. Nothing else moves. There are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge on this trip (EV-FARE-00104), so POL-RD-09 adds no pass-through correction and produces no billing-integrity referral; the driver's own POL-RD-09 claim was discarded for not disclosing the impairment of the advisory it cited. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises (deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips - no pattern). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifier TRP-00104 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (10-second sampling, zero gaps); no timestamps conflict; and no charge line is unmatched. 8. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight 1.0 of the artifacts that carry the decision (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01). The $3.60 refund is at or below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold and is executed on issue; fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is set to 3.60. Either party may appeal once, within 30 days, through the help channel.
To the rider and the driver. Outcome: the rider is refunded SGD 3.60 of the SGD 43.41 charged (PARTIAL_REFUND). The charge stands in every other respect. 1. The trace and the excess. GPS trace EV-GPS-00104 is complete — 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no escalation arises under POL-RD-10(3). The governing measurement is the trace distance 34.17 km (POL-RD-01), not the rounded 34.2 km convenience copy on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 27.1 km on EV-TRIP-00104 the excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09%; both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip id TRP-00104 matches across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 20:35:10 matches the recorded start. 2. The closure excuses part of it. LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link — a road the booked optimal route uses — with a 20:02–21:35 window covering the trip, and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE. POL-RD-03 therefore applies. The cap is min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so 4.90 km of the 7.07 km is excused and the driver is not penalised for avoiding a HIGH-severity closure. 3. Why NO_ACTION is not the outcome. The driver's advocate argues that once the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km is used, the residual excess of 2.17 km is only 6.8% and fails POL-RD-01's percentage limb, so nothing is payable. I do not accept that. The deviation is established on the trace's measured excess against the booked optimal; POL-RD-02 applies where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause FULLY excuses it, and POL-RD-03 excuses only 4.90 of the 7.07 km; and POL-RD-03 itself directs that the excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route. The adjusted optimal is the figure the refund is computed on, not a device that erases the deviation. Both advocates in fact agree the arithmetic lands at SGD 3.60. 4. The arithmetic. fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. With the closure-adjusted optimal route of 32.00 km and 40.1 minutes (the booked 34.0 minutes scaled by 32.00/27.1, the amended duration being null), and the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-00104: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828. Refund = charged_total 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and at 8.25% of the charge it is far below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. The rider's SGD 14.00 is her estimate of the difference from her usual fare; the figure the record supports is SGD 3.60. 5. Claims answered. (a) The driver's account that the diversion was occasioned by the closure is accepted so far as the capped 4.90 km goes, carried by EV-ADVIS-00104-01. (b) The chat log does not move money to the driver or excuse distance: the only route proposal in EV-CHAT-00104 is the driver's own message at 20:38:12, and the rider's reply 'ok but not too long ah' names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are not met and no distance is excluded on that ground. (c) The CTE advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired (weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE) and describes a corridor this trip never enters; it excuses nothing, and because an advisory for this trip is on file and relied on, POL-RD-13 confirms this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. (d) No POL-RD-06 conduct referral or uplift: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, and the excess (7.07 km / 26.09%) is below both materiality gates (8.0 km / 50%); the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and forms no part of this decision. (e) No billing-integrity referral: EV-FARE-00104 carries no ERP lines and no airport surcharge, and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. (f) No POL-RD-10 trigger fires — the three artifacts carry matching trip identifiers, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, the refund is far below SGD 150, and no charge line is unmatched — so the case is ruled on the merits. 6. Discarded material. One claim on the driver's side was discarded by the citation referee and is recorded below; it is not a ground of this ruling. 7. Confidence, referral and execution. Confidence is 0.9, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01 and EV-FARE-00104). No clause produces a referral. The refund of SGD 3.60 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
Rider and driver, here is the ruling. The deviation is made out on the platform's own telemetry. EV-GPS-00104 records 34.17 km between pickup and dropoff and the platform's booked optimal was 27.1 km (EV-TRIP-00104). That is 7.07 km more than optimal, or 26.09%, which clears both of POL-RD-01's establishment tests (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km), so a route deviation is established. The governing figure is the trace, not the rounded 34.2 km on the trip record. The driver's closure excuse is partly good. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 is an LTA DataMall accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link (the corridor the booked optimal uses), in force 20:02-21:35 on 16 July 2026, covering the time the vehicle would have reached that segment within POL-RD-03's 15-minute buffer, and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked stretch and rejoins on the AYE. Under POL-RD-03 that exonerates the driver, but only up to the cap: min(measured 7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from 34.0 min to 40.1 min. The excess beyond the cap is what the rider recovers. POL-RD-03 provides that the excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 prescribes the same treatment where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess. The arithmetic is: charged_total = 43.41 recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 39.828 refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, payable rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.60. To the rider: your $14 figure is not the measure. The PIE accident is real and documented and the driver was entitled to avoid it; most of the extra distance and time is explained by the closure and is not refundable. What is refundable is the 2.17 km he drove beyond even the closure-adjusted route (34.17 - 32.00), and that is the SGD 3.60. The fare is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. To the driver: I reject the argument that, once POL-RD-03 is applied, the remaining 2.17 km (6.8% of the adjusted optimal) fails the percentage limb and no deviation exists. POL-RD-03 itself says the excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal, and POL-RD-02 says to run against the adjusted optimal where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess. The establishment tests were met on the measured trace; the cap limits the exoneration, it does not erase the deviation. On the remaining points. POL-RD-04 does not apply: the only route proposal in EV-CHAT-00104 is the driver's own at 20:38:12, and the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so no distance is excluded as a rider-requested detour. The second advisory, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is impaired (weight 0.25; issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE) and describes a CTE corridor this trip never enters, so it excuses nothing and reduces no part of the excess; no part of this ruling rests on it, so it does not move the confidence cap. No POL-RD-06 pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d is 1 over 288 trips), so there is no uplift and no conduct referral, and the lifetime field prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day counter the clause names. POL-RD-09 finds nothing to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and the trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no billing-integrity finding. POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10 are not engaged: the trace has 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0; trip id TRP-00104 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; and no timestamps conflict. No driver compensation arises, because the billed distance (34.2 km) is not less than the trace distance (34.17 km). The ruling rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01), so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence is stated at 0.85. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue.
